prompt_en: A wide staged editorial photograph of a complex religious and mythic test scene in a contemporary black-box theater. At center, a fictional adult woman, explicitly a 28-year-old performer portraying a deceased soul, stands beside an open upright funerary coffin. The supplied portrait guides only the visible facial proportions, rounded dark eyes, soft lips, and dark chin-length bob with wispy fringe. Her ivory satin stage dress and still, alert bearing give her a quietly magnetic presence. She deliberately holds her place before the balance. One waist-high brass Egyptian judgment balance stands immediately before her. Its left pan holds her ceramic red anatomical-heart prop, its right pan holds one upright white feather of Maat; the beam is level. A jackal-headed adult Anubis performer touches the balance's central plumb line while watching both pans. An ibis-headed adult Thoth performer writes this same balanced outcome with a reed pen on an angled papyrus tablet bearing a small heart-and-feather balance diagram. The woman, coffin, and heart share a distinct blue cartouche medallion. Behind her the admission arch is open and warmly lit, showing the favorable judgment's route toward the upper realm. Across the foreground, three distinct adult Moirai performers handle one thick crimson life-thread: Clotho draws it from flax onto a spindle, Lachesis stretches the next segment along a marked measuring rod, and Atropos closes silver shears on its far end, with two freshly severed tips close beside the blades. The connected course from spindle to rod to the cutting point is fully visible; beyond the small cut gap, the same crimson strand continues to the deceased woman's medallion. A single sculptural world-axis tree fills the rear stage, its continuous trunk rising from a visible dark subterranean root chamber through an inhabited earth platform into a celestial crown under a luminous star canopy. The same tree visibly connects all three vertically separated realms. Three separated foreground workstations keep Clotho's spindle, Lachesis's marked rod, and Atropos's closing blades plainly visible; a slightly raised frontal camera holds all six performers, both scale pans, the tree roots, and crown crisp in the same frame. Warm facial light reveals satin folds, feather barbs, and taut fiber.
